title: A facile and green method for synthesis of ZnFe2O4@CMC as a new magnetic nanophotocatalyst for ciprofloxacin removal from aqueous media
author: Malakootian, Nasiri, et al.
materials: Ciprofloxacin (99%) was obtained from Temad Pharmaceutical Company (Tehran, Iran), and CMC was purchased from Sigma-Aldrich Company (USA). Other chemicals such as Fe(NO3)3·9H2O, Zn(NO3)2·6H2O, HCl, NaOH, acetonitrile, acetic acid, methanol, and ethanol were obtained from Merck Company (Germany). All the materials were in analytical grade and used without further purification. All the aqueous solutions were prepared using distilled water.

steps.title: Prepare metal nitrate solution
steps.instruction: Weigh 8.06 g of Fe(NO₃)₃·9H₂O and 2.96 g of Zn(NO₃)₂·6H₂O (2:1 molar ratio) and dissolve them in 100 mL of deionized water in a beaker.

steps.title: Add carboxymethyl cellulose
steps.instruction: Add 0.5 g of carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) to the metal nitrate solution and stir vigorously at room temperature until a homogeneous suspension is obtained.

steps.title: Adjust pH with NaOH
steps.instruction: Gradually add 6 g of NaOH to the suspension over the course of one hour while continuing to stir, until the pH reaches 12 and the mixture turns brown.

steps.title: Hydrothermal treatment
steps.instruction: Transfer the brown suspension to a sealed vessel and place it in an oven set to 160 °C for 20 h.

steps.title: Wash and dry the product
steps.instruction: After cooling, collect the precipitate, wash it repeatedly with distilled water followed by ethanol, then dry the solid at 60 °C for 2 h.

steps.title: Characterize the nanophotocatalyst (optional)
steps.instruction: Perform XRD (2θ = 20°–80°), FESEM‑EDS, TEM (150 kV), FT‑IR, VSM, UV‑DRS, BET (N₂ adsorption at 120 °C), and elemental mapping as described in the article to confirm structure and properties.

steps.title: Set up the photoreactor
steps.instruction: Use a borosilicate glass batch reactor (internal dimensions: length 25 cm, width 10 cm, height 5 cm) equipped with three 6 W UV‑C lamps (Philips), a mechanical stirrer, and a cooling water jacket to maintain constant temperature.

steps.title: Prepare ciprofloxacin test solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve ciprofloxacin (CIP) in distilled water to obtain the desired initial concentration (choose among 5, 10, 20, 30 mg L⁻¹). Adjust the solution pH to the required value (3, 5, 7, 9, 11) using HCl or NaOH.

steps.title: Add catalyst and set loading
steps.instruction: Add the required amount of ZnFe₂O₄@CMC (0.1, 0.2, 0.3, or 0.5 g) to the CIP solution in the reactor and start the mechanical stirrer.

steps.title: Run control experiments
steps.instruction: For photolysis control, irradiate the CIP solution with the UV lamps but omit the catalyst. For adsorption control, keep the mixture in the dark with the catalyst present.

steps.title: Perform photocatalytic degradation
steps.instruction: Irradiate the stirred mixture with the three UV lamps for the selected reaction time (20, 40, 60, 80, 100, or 120 min). The optimal condition reported is 0.3 g catalyst, pH 7, CIP 5 mg L⁻¹, and 100 min irradiation.

steps.title: Sample at defined intervals
steps.instruction: At predetermined times, withdraw an aliquot, separate ZnFe₂O₄@CMC from the liquid using an external magnet, and keep the supernatant for analysis.

steps.title: Analyze CIP concentration by HPLC
steps.instruction: Inject 60 µL of each filtered sample into an HPLC (Waters E600) equipped with a UV detector set at 272 nm. Use a C18 column (250 mm × 4.6 mm, 5 µm) with a mobile phase of water/methanol/acetonitrile/1 % acetic acid (15/15/20/50 v/v) at a flow rate of 0.5 mL min⁻¹.

steps.title: Measure total organic carbon
steps.instruction: Determine TOC of each sample with a Shimadzu TOC‑VCSH analyzer.

steps.title: Calculate degradation efficiency
steps.instruction: Use the formula % degradation = 100 × (C₀ − C_t)/C₀, where C₀ is the initial CIP concentration and C_t is the concentration at time t measured by HPLC.

steps.title: Perform kinetic analysis
steps.instruction: Fit the concentration data to the pseudo‑first‑order model Ln(C_t/C₀) = −K_obs t and to the Langmuir‑Hinshelwood model 1/K_obs = 1/(K_c K_L‑H) + C₀/(K_c K_L‑H), extracting K_obs, K_c and K_L‑H as described.

steps.title: Test real wastewater
steps.instruction: Collect wastewater from the campus sewerage network and adjust it to contain CIP 4.5 mg L⁻¹ (COD 415 mg L⁻¹, BOD 247 mg L⁻¹). Perform the photocatalytic run under the previously determined optimal conditions.

steps.title: Evaluate catalyst reusability
steps.instruction: After each photocatalytic run, recover ZnFe₂O₄@CMC with a magnet, wash it with an alcohol/water mixture, dry it at 100 °C, and reuse it for up to five consecutive cycles, recording CIP removal efficiency each time.

steps.title: Assess chemical stability
steps.instruction: After the fifth cycle, record XRD patterns of the recovered catalyst to check for structural changes. Measure dissolved Fe and Zn ions in the final reaction solution by atomic absorption spectroscopy (AAS‑PG 990) at 248.3 nm (Fe) and 213.9 nm (Zn).
